shared_header_format.layout: 8 little-endian uint32 words, parsed by src/fnr3_re/xdb.py::parse_xdb_header
proven_facts: Identical 8-word shape observed in all 10 decoded members with zero exceptions.
word2, word3, and word4 are numerically equal in 9 of 10 tables; xdbtrain.adf is the one exception (word2=5288, word3=word4=7200), proving these are not always three redundant copies of one field.

word4 equals the decoded payload size exactly in 2 of 10 tables (xdbevent.adf, xdbrivl.adf); in the other 8 it is smaller than the payload by a per-table remainder (see per_table entries), consistent with a trailing region (e.g. a string pool) after a fixed-size leading section.
word6 is non-zero only in xdbboxr.adf (21) and xdbcutpn.adf (16389); word7 is non-zero only in xdbvenue.adf, xdbalias.adf, and xdbhmtwn.adf.
unresolved: Whether word0 or word1 is a record count, a field/column count, a string-table entry count, or something else -- neither interpretation produces an integer (word2-32)/count stride for more than 2 of the 10 tables, so this cannot be settled by arithmetic alone.
The meaning of the word5/word6/word7 trailing words when non-zero.
The exact meaning and boundary of the 'trailing_bytes' region in the 8 tables where word4 < payload size.

tables.notes: Highest-priority table; see xdbboxr-schema.json and boxer-ownership-map.json for what static evidence adds beyond this shared header.
word0=9 is consistent with a small fixed venue list; not confirmed.

The 404-byte body after the header is a dense run of small 16-bit fields including a strictly-increasing sequential index (1..50 observed by inspection); no string data appears anywhere in the decoded payload. This is a numeric cross-reference/index-style table, not a boxer-style named-record table. Not reduced to an exact field schema in this pass.
word0=5 is consistent with a small fixed hometown/region list ('hmtwn'); not confirmed.

word0=59 and word1=61 are close in value, unlike most other tables where word1 is much larger than word0; plausibly consistent with a rivalry list sized near the roster (see xdbboxr.adf's own word0=121), but not confirmed.
The only table where section_size_a disagrees with section_size_b/c -- proves these three words are not always redundant copies of one field.

word1=239 matches xdbtrain.adf's word1 exactly; both are consumed by contract/contracts.viv's trainer.fnc/cutman.fnc side of the game (training staff and cut personnel), a plausible but unconfirmed cross-table relationship.
